title: Notre Dame scores in the fifth minute to end Mississippi State’s shutout streak and NCAA run
excerpt: Bristol Kersh ended the Bulldogs’ shutout streak at 495 minutes, 39 seconds. Mississippi State put eight shots on target after halftime in the 4–0 loss.
locality: Starkville, Mississippi, and South Bend, Indiana.

The Irish went on to win 4–0 in South Bend, Indiana, knocking the Bulldogs out in the second round. Mississippi State finishes the season 10–3–7.

paragraphs.text: Bristol Kersh scored 4 minutes, 13 seconds into Friday’s NCAA tournament game at Notre Dame, ending a Mississippi State shutout streak that dated to Oct. 15. The Irish went on to win 4–0 in South Bend, Indiana, knocking the Bulldogs out in the second round. Mississippi State finishes the season 10–3–7.

Mississippi State goalkeeper Jenny Harrison stopped a shot by Kersh at 3:47. Twenty-six seconds later, Kersh put the Irish ahead with an unassisted goal. The Bulldogs had entered the night 8:34 short of 500 consecutive scoreless minutes. Kersh stopped the clock on that streak at 495 minutes, 39 seconds.

Morgan Roy doubled the lead at 17:12, with Grace Restovich and Lily Joseph credited with assists. Restovich set up another goal 11 minutes into the second half, this time for Izzy Engle, who scored her 12th of the season. Charlie Codd made it 4–0 with an unassisted goal at 65:38.

The Bulldogs took 16 of their 22 shots after halftime. Eight of those second-half attempts reached the goal, and Notre Dame saved all eight. At the other end, Harrison made 11 saves before Sarah Wommack came on and added one. Notre Dame put 16 of its 28 attempts on target.

It was the first time in six games that an opponent had scored on Mississippi State during play. The Bulldogs had held Auburn, LSU, Alabama, Texas and Samford scoreless. Texas advanced on penalty kicks after a 0–0 draw in the SEC tournament. A 2–0 win over Samford in Starkville took State through the opening round of the NCAA tournament.
